judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending S.J.Res. 24 to the President to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the northern long-eared bat as endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The House passed it 220-209.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending S.J.Res. 24 to the President to cancel the Fish and Wildlife Service rule listing the northern long-eared bat as endangered, removing its Endangered Species Act protection. The House passed it 220-209.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 1435, which barred the federal environmental agency from granting California the Clean Air Act permission it needs to require rising shares of zero-emission new vehicles. The House passed it 222-190.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 1435, which barred the federal environmental agency from granting California the Clean Air Act permission it needs to require rising shares of zero-emission new vehicles. The House passed it 222-190.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 32 to cancel the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule requiring lenders to collect and report data on small business lending, including to women-owned and minority-owned firms. The Senate passed it 53-44.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 32 to cancel the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule requiring lenders to collect and report data on small business lending, including to women-owned and minority-owned firms. The Senate passed it 53-44.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 42, which would overturn federal protections against sexual-orientation and gender-identity discrimination in food programs. The Senate rejected it 47-50, so it did not become law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 42, which would overturn federal protections against sexual-orientation and gender-identity discrimination in food programs. The Senate rejected it 47-50, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for S.J.Res. 43, which would cancel the Education Department's SAVE plan, the student loan plan that lowered payments based on income. The Senate rejected it 49-50, so it did not become law.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against S.J.Res. 43, which would cancel the Education Department's SAVE plan, the student loan plan that lowered payments based on income. The Senate rejected it 49-50, so it did not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 5283, which barred the federal government from using federal land to house immigrants who entered without legal permission. The House passed it 224-203.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 5283, which barred the federal government from using federal land to house immigrants who entered without legal permission. The House passed it 224-203.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for sending S.J.Res. 32 to the President to cancel the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule requiring lenders to collect and report data on small business lending, including to women-owned and minority-owned firms. The House passed it 221-202.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against sending S.J.Res. 32 to the President to cancel the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule requiring lenders to collect and report data on small business lending, including to women-owned and minority-owned firms. The House passed it 221-202.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 4468, which barred the federal environmental agency from setting tailpipe emission standards that would push automakers toward mostly electric fleets. The House passed it 221-197.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 4468, which barred the federal environmental agency from setting tailpipe emission standards that would push automakers toward mostly electric fleets. The House passed it 221-197.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 88 to cancel the Education Department's SAVE plan, the student loan plan that lowered payments based on income. The House passed it 210-189.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 88 to cancel the Education Department's SAVE plan, the student loan plan that lowered payments based on income. The House passed it 210-189.

judgments.yea_description: Voted yes for the final House-Senate deal on H.R. 2670 for fiscal year 2024, which set defense policy and approved Defense Department programs and military construction. The House passed it 310-118.
judgments.nay_description: Voted no on the final House-Senate deal on H.R. 2670 for fiscal year 2024, which set defense policy and approved Defense Department programs and military construction. The House passed it 310-118.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.J.Res. 98 to cancel the National Labor Relations Board rule making it easier to treat two companies, such as a franchisor and its franchisee, as joint employers of the same workers. The House passed it 206-177.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.J.Res. 98 to cancel the National Labor Relations Board rule making it easier to treat two companies, such as a franchisor and its franchisee, as joint employers of the same workers. The House passed it 206-177.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 5585, the Agent Raul Gonzalez Officer Safety Act, which set required prison terms for fleeing Border Patrol by vehicle within 100 miles of the border and made immigrants convicted of it subject to removal. The House passed it 271-154.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 5585, the Agent Raul Gonzalez Officer Safety Act, which set required prison terms for fleeing Border Patrol by vehicle within 100 miles of the border and made immigrants convicted of it subject to removal. The House passed it 271-154.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 6678, the Consequences for Social Security Fraud Act, which made Social Security or identification document fraud a ground for barring an immigrant from entering the country and for deporting one already here. The House passed it 272-155.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 6678, the Consequences for Social Security Fraud Act, which made Social Security or identification document fraud a ground for barring an immigrant from entering the country and for deporting one already here. The House passed it 272-155.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 6976, the Protect Our Communities from DUIs Act, which made driving while intoxicated or impaired a ground for barring an immigrant from entering the country and for deporting one already here. The House passed it 274-150.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 6976, the Protect Our Communities from DUIs Act, which made driving while intoxicated or impaired a ground for barring an immigrant from entering the country and for deporting one already here. The House passed it 274-150.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for H.R. 7176, the Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act, which ended Energy Department reviews of natural gas imports and exports and put federal energy regulators alone in charge of liquefied natural gas terminals. The House passed it 224-200.
judgments.nay_description: Voted against H.R. 7176, the Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act, which ended Energy Department reviews of natural gas imports and exports and put federal energy regulators alone in charge of liquefied natural gas terminals. The House passed it 224-200.
